title: perf(canary): automated detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Alex Kim
description:
Motivation: We need continuous, automated detection of latency and throughput regressions in the perf-canary pipeline and automated rollout guards so we can safely promote model/runtime changes to production without manual babysitting. This PR implements a statistically-driven detector, hysteresis-based rollout guards, and operator-friendly alerts/dashboards.

Summary of changes: Adds a new detector service (perf-canary-detector) that ingests per-route latency and token throughput metrics from the canary runner, computes windowed baseline distributions, and flags significant regressions using a combination of moving-percentile baselines and Student's t/z statistics with configurable sample sizes. Introduces rollout guard policies that can be attached to any rollout: immediate-block, delayed-block-with-auto-rollback, and advisory-only. Implements hysteresis and minimum-sample safeguards to avoid flapping on transient spikes. Adds migration and config schema for rollout policies, new dashboard panels, and end-to-end integration tests in the perf-canary CI pipeline.

Why this approach: Existing threshold-based checks produced many false positives during cold-starts and high-variance workloads. The detector uses a hybrid baseline (recent median + long-term 95th percentile) and requires both statistical significance and minimum-effect-size before raising a fail. Hysteresis requires the condition to persist across N consecutive windows (configurable) before enforcing an automated rollback. This balances sensitivity and stability for production rollouts.

Compatibility and rollout: The default policy is advisory-only for 1 week to gather signal; infra can opt-in to block-promote for critical routes. Backwards-compatible: old rollouts without policies behave the same. Config is stored in the rollout record and supports per-route overrides.

Testing and validation: See commits and CI checks for unit tests of the detector, fixture-based integration tests that replay synthetic regression traces, and end-to-end perf pipeline runs that validate false-positive rate against historical traces. Benchmarks show the detector running at ~120 samples/sec on a single t3 small service worker (negligible cost relative to canary runner).

Notes: This PR touches critical control-paths for rollouts—please review the rollout guard logic and alert wording carefully.

review_comments:
Priya Sharma (review): Can you clarify the choice of a hybrid baseline (recent median + long-term 95th)? How does this behave for routes with non-stationary latency (e.g. seasonal traffic)?

Alex: We picked the hybrid baseline to quickly adapt to gradual shifts (median) while keeping protection from long-term trends (95th). For non-stationary routes we recommend raising the min-sample and shortening window durations; I added notes in docs with recommended presets for bursty routes.

Liam O'Connor (request changes): The auto-rollback path calls the rollout API directly — we need auth checks and an audit event. Also add a safety TTL before a rollback can be triggered.

Alex: Added enforcement to require a 'can_autorollback' flag on the rollout record and emit an audit record. TTL configurable via policy; default 10 minutes. Updated tests to cover TTL behavior.

Maya Chen (nit): small naming nit in metrics aggregation helper (PercentileWindow -> SlidingPercentile).

Alex: Renamed and pushed a follow-up commit to keep naming consistent.
